text: its not that water is below the ground. that is expected. its that there is a wedge of open air between the ground and the water

events.text: REVERTED in 751626804 — this wedge fix over-corrected into a 'jello brick' that didn't read as water; restored the original look. Crack to be re-addressed minimally.

resolution: Two follow-ups on painted water after the fall-through fix landed. (1) WEDGE OF AIR: floorToWaterBody dropped the water surface straight to the basin floor 'base' at the first DRY cell, so the heightfield surface ramped downward right at the wet/dry boundary while the dug terrain wall rose upward — leaving a triangular open-air gap between the water's edge and the wall. Fixed by dilating the flat surface 2 cells into the surrounding dry ring (WATER_SURFACE_DILATE), tucking that downward skirt UNDER the higher opaque terrain so the waterline meets the wall cleanly; the surface is also forced flat (one fill level) since water is flat, not per-cell. Recessed-below-ground pools are intended and untouched. (2) INVISIBLE WAVES: bumped WATER_WAVE amplitude 0.1->0.25, length 5->4, speed 0.22->0.32 so the ripple actually reads, including in a recessed basin. Both editor (rippleWaterField) and compiled (encodeWaterBodies ships the same field + WATER_WAVE header) consume these; editor hot-reloads, compiled needs only a game bake, no loader rebuild. 6/6 water tests pass.
